rule_contents.description: How the platform selects the approach for each season (cycle), target and product from the historical and validation evidence (scripts/method_selection.py, docs/50). Fixed before further validation seasons are scored. A selection is the approach the evidence supports; the published forecast changes only by an explicit decision.

probabilities.label: Published tercile probabilities
probabilities.score: RPS of the tercile probabilities (lower is better)

amounts.label: Rainfall amounts (and ranges)
amounts.score: CRPS of the rainfall-amount forecast in mm (lower is better)

rule_contents.historical: A method is a candidate for a target and product only if its benchmark confirms it better than the published reference: outer leave-one-year-out over the training years (1993-2016), Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.05 (false discovery rate) across every method and target of its family, and not worse over the test years (2017 onward).

changes.note: Decided by the project lead after the sensitivity analyses (33-year and pooled evidence, Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg) had been seen; the decisions are recomputed from the p-values each benchmark stored, within the same families. The benchmarks keep their own Holm decisions as run.

changes.change: Practical tie rule: candidates within 1% of the published score are tied; the simplest is selected
changes.note: Decided by the project lead before the re-scored second-stage results are known.

validation.rule: Independent validation seasons are forecast years scored after the benchmark (bias_validation.py for bias correction; dist_shadow.py for the EMOS amount model). A candidate becomes 'recommended' once at least minimum_seasons have been scored for it and the reference and its mean score over them is not worse; with fewer it stays a 'candidate'; with enough and a worse mean it is 'not supported by validation'. A candidate with no validation record yet needs a shadow forecast before it can be recommended.

rule_contents.choice: Among candidates, a recommended one first; then the candidate with the largest training-period improvement over the reference, unless the practical tie rule (tie_rule) applies. One change at a time: candidates from different families (e.g. an amount correction and a probability calibration) were each tested against the published approach, not together, so the selection changes one stage only; the others are listed as alternatives.

tie_rule.rule: Candidates of the same status whose training-period improvement is within 1% of the published approach's own training-period score (CRPS of the MVS ensemble for amounts, RPS of the published probabilities for probabilities, All Ethiopia) of the largest improvement are tied; the simplest tied candidate is selected, and the tie is recorded.
simplicity_order: Phase 3 distribution models (BJP, BMA, QRF), Leung–Dirichlet calibration, statistical downscaling (CCA, PCR)
tie_rule.reason: A negligible difference does not displace a simpler, better-understood method: 1% is above the largest error of the earlier numerical CRPS (0.7%, scripts/crps_precision.py) and well below the typical confirmed improvements (3–8%).
tie_rule.decided: 2026-10-20 by the project lead, before the second-stage re-scoring of the close JJAS September comparison

statuses.keep: Keep the published approach: no method is confirmed better on the historical evidence.
statuses.candidate: Confirmed better on the historical evidence; independent validation seasons are still being collected.
statuses.recommended: Confirmed better on the historical evidence and not worse over the independent validation seasons.
statuses.not_supported: Confirmed better on the historical evidence but worse over the independent validation seasons.
